religion_basis: survey estimate: self-identification, Spanish citizens aged 18+ entitled to vote in the regional election
religion_note: CIS study 3558, the pre-electoral survey for the 2026 election to the Parliament of Andalusia, fieldwork 10-18 April 2026: "¿Cómo se define Ud. en materia religiosa: católico/a practicante, católico/a no practicante, creyente de otra religión, agnóstico/a, indiferente o no creyente, o ateo/a?" Answers as the CIS offers them; its N.C. (no answer) is Not stated. A survey estimate, not a count: 8,017 respondents in Andalucía (telephone interviews (CATI) with quotas of sex and age, weighted by the CIS's coefficients for the comunidad (PESO); these are its published weighted shares). Universe: Spanish citizens aged 18 and over resident in Andalucía and entitled to vote in its election, so foreign residents, among whom Muslims and Orthodox Christians are many, are not in it. The question records the religion people identify with, practising or not; surveys that first ask whether one belongs to any religion at all, such as the European Social Survey, find fewer Catholics and more people with none. No Spanish census since the Constitution of 1978, which provides that no one may be obliged to declare their religion (art. 16.2), has asked it, and the CIS's monthly barometers publish it by no region.

Read from the CIS's PDF marginals for La Rioja as its former website published them, captured by the Internet Archive on 4 February 2020: the study's page on the CIS's current site links them to pages that no longer answer. The province of La Rioja is the whole of La Rioja, so these are the comunidad's figures. Universe: Spanish citizens aged 18 and over resident in La Rioja and entitled to vote in general elections, so foreign residents, among whom Muslims and Orthodox Christians are many, are not in it. The question records the religion people identify with, practising or not; surveys that first ask whether one belongs to any religion at all, such as the European Social Survey, find fewer Catholics and more people with none. No Spanish census since the Constitution of 1978, which provides that no one may be obliged to declare their religion (art. 16.2), has asked it, and the CIS's monthly barometers publish it by no region.
